data.label: Head Unit
data.description: The main processing unit of the infotainment system.

data.label: Touch Display
data.description: The primary user interface for the infotainment system.

data.label: Audio System
data.description: Handles audio output for the infotainment system.

data.label: Smartphone
data.description: External device for app projection and Bluetooth.

data.label: Storage
data.description: Main storage for the infotainment system.

data.label: Secure Storage
data.description: Area for storing sensitive data securely.

data.label: Bootloader
data.description: The initial program that runs when the system powers on.

data.label: Navigation Data
data.description: Stores navigation map data and routes.

Derivations.name: CWE-306: Authentication in Security Decision -> CAPEC-27: Malicious File Loading -> MITRE ATT&CK T1059.001: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell -> ATM: Removable Media
Derivations.loss: Execution of unauthorized code via USB storage
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker inserts a malicious USB drive, leveraging vulnerabilities in the USB driver stack to execute arbitrary code on the Head Unit.

Derivations.name: CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management -> CAPEC-28: Privilege Escalation -> MITRE ATT&CK T1548.002: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Via Setuid and Setgid -> ATM: Control of System
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker exploits a privilege escalation vulnerability in the Head Unit's operating system to gain administrative control and modify critical system settings.

Derivations.name: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor -> CAPEC-29: Data Leakage -> MITRE ATT&CK T1071.001: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols -> ATM: Gather Target Information
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker uses Bluetooth to scan for and exfiltrate sensitive data from connected devices or the infotainment system.

Derivations.name: CWE-306: Authentication in Security Decision -> CAPEC-28: Privilege Escalation -> MITRE ATT&CK T1071.001: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols -> ATM: Network Sniffing
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the WiFi stack to intercept and analyze unencrypted traffic, potentially capturing sensitive data like credentials.

Derivations.name: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials -> CAPEC-15: Logic Bomb -> MITRE ATT&CK T1078: Valid Accounts -> ATM: Spoofing Location
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker manipulates the GPS signal, providing false location data to the navigation system, leading to incorrect routing or tracking.

Derivations.name: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor -> CAPEC-29: Data Leakage -> MITRE ATT&CK T1572: Protocol Tunneling -> ATM: Telematics Data Exfiltration
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker compromises the Telematics Control Unit to exfiltrate sensitive vehicle or user data transmitted through the telematics channel.

Derivations.name: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type -> CAPEC-28: Privilege Escalation -> MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application -> ATM: App Projection Manipulation
Derivations.loss: Unauthorized control of vehicle functions via app projection
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker manipulates the app projection from a compromised smartphone to gain unauthorized control over infotainment features or potentially other vehicle systems.

Derivations.name: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials -> CAPEC-15: Logic Bomb -> MITRE ATT&CK T1555.003: Credentials from Web Browsers -> ATM: OTA Package Tampering
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker compromises the cloud backend to distribute a tampered OTA update package, leading to the installation of malware on the Head Unit.

Derivations.name: CWE-15: External Control of System or Configuration Setting -> CAPEC-64: Bus Spoofer -> MITRE ATT&CK T1071.004: Application Layer Protocol: DNS -> ATM: CAN Bus Injection
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker injects malicious messages into the vehicle's CAN bus network, potentially affecting safety-critical systems.

Derivations.name: CWE-284: Improper Access Control -> CAPEC-64: Bus Spoofer -> MITRE ATT&CK T1071.004: Application Layer Protocol: DNS -> ATM: CAN Bus Injection
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker exploits vulnerabilities in the CAN transceiver to inject unauthorized CAN messages, disrupting vehicle operation.

Derivations.name: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') -> CAPEC-20: Cross-Site Scripting -> MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application -> ATM: Network Intrusion
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker exploits vulnerabilities in the Ethernet interface to gain unauthorized access to the infotainment system's network.

Derivations.name: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor -> CAPEC-29: Data Leakage -> MITRE ATT&CK T1081: Credentials In Files -> ATM: Data Exfiltration from Storage
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker gains unauthorized access to the infotainment system's storage and exfiltrates sensitive data such as user profiles or media files.

Derivations.name: CWE-119: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer -> CAPEC-13: Input Validation Deception -> MITRE ATT&CK T1574.002: Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Side-Loading -> ATM: Firmware Tampering
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker modifies the firmware stored in the Code Flash, potentially installing malicious code or altering system behavior.

Derivations.name: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information -> CAPEC-29: Data Leakage -> MITRE ATT&CK T1081: Credentials In Files -> ATM: Sensitive Data Exposure
Derivations.loss: Exposure of sensitive data in Data Flash
Derivations.damage_scene: Sensitive information stored in the Data Flash is accessed and exposed due to weak security controls or cleartext storage.

Derivations.name: CWE-316: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in Memory -> CAPEC-29: Data Leakage -> MITRE ATT&CK T1552.001: Steal or Substitute Credentials: Plaintext Accesses and Information -> ATM: Secure Storage Compromise
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker bypasses security mechanisms to access and extract sensitive data stored in the Secure Storage.

Derivations.name: CWE-320: Key Management System Vulnerabilities -> CAPEC-16: Key Compromise -> MITRE ATT&CK T1552.001: Steal or Substitute Credentials: Plaintext Accesses and Information -> ATM: Key Theft
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker steals cryptographic keys stored within the system, enabling decryption of sensitive data or impersonation.

Derivations.name: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature -> CAPEC-16: Key Compromise -> MITRE ATT&CK T1553.002: Subvert Trust Controls: Install Root Certificate -> ATM: Certificate Forgery
Derivations.loss: Forgery or misuse of digital certificates
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker compromises or forges digital certificates, allowing them to impersonate legitimate entities or bypass trust mechanisms.

Derivations.name: CWE-120: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow') -> CAPEC-13: Input Validation Deception -> MITRE ATT&CK T1547.001: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder -> ATM: Bootloader Tampering
Derivations.loss: Execution of unauthorized code during boot
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the bootloader to load and execute malicious code when the system powers on, compromising the entire system.

Derivations.name: CWE-1295: Debug Messages Revealing Unnecessary Information -> CAPEC-15: Logic Bomb -> MITRE ATT&CK T1059.003: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell -> ATM: Debug Port Abuse
Derivations.loss: Unauthorized access and control via debug port
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker leverages the debug port to gain unauthorized access and execute commands, potentially controlling the system or exfiltrating data.

Derivations.name: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor -> CAPEC-29: Data Leakage -> MITRE ATT&CK T1081: Credentials In Files -> ATM: User Profile Theft
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker accesses and steals user profile data, including personal information and preferences, leading to privacy violations.

Derivations.name: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials -> CAPEC-16: Key Compromise -> MITRE ATT&CK T1552.001: Steal or Substitute Credentials: Plaintext Accesses and Information -> ATM: Credential Harvesting
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker obtains user credentials stored within the system, enabling them to impersonate users or gain unauthorized access to accounts.

Derivations.name: CWE-1097: Persistent Storable Data Element without Associated Comparison Control Element -> CAPEC-15: Logic Bomb -> MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011: Signed Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32 -> ATM: Navigation Data Tampering
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker modifies navigation data, causing incorrect routing, location spoofing, or denial of navigation services.

Derivations.name: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type -> CAPEC-20: Cross-Site Scripting -> MITRE ATT&CK T1083: File and Directory Discovery -> ATM: Media File Corruption
Derivations.loss: Corruption or manipulation of media files
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker corrupts or manipulates media files stored in the infotainment system, leading to playback issues or potential execution of malicious code.

Derivations.name: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor -> CAPEC-29: Data Leakage -> MITRE ATT&CK T1081: Credentials In Files -> ATM: Application Data Exfiltration
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker accesses and exfiltrates sensitive data associated with installed applications, potentially revealing user activity or configuration details.

Derivations.name: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature -> CAPEC-16: Key Compromise -> MITRE ATT&CK T1554: Compromise Infrastructure -> ATM: Malicious OTA Package Installation
Derivations.damage_scene: An attacker crafts a malicious OTA package with a forged signature and tricks the system into installing it, leading to system compromise.
